##**Load Packages
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

##**Loading Data Made in Last Rmd
```{r}
data.02 <- read_csv("data/clean.dt.elk.data.02.csv")
```

##**Creating New Observations at >30 mins (1800s)
```{r}
new.obs <- data.02 %>%
  group_by(location) %>%
  # This mutate adds a new column "observation" to capture the number of 
  # obsservations within a camera. Since you already grouped by camera, it should
  # operate by camera. The cumsum function goes sequentially throuhg all rows
  # and asks if time_diff is greater than 1800. If it is, it gets a new
  # observation number, so each observation greater than 1800 seconds becomes
  # a new observation until the next new observation is encountered. I've also 
  # added 1 to the cumsum because the first observation number is zero.
  mutate(observation = cumsum(time_diff > 1800 & !is.na(time_diff)) + 1)

```

##**Visualizing Data
```{r}
ggplot(new.obs, aes(x = hour, colour = time_period, fill = time_period)) +
  geom_density (alpha = 0.2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Hour of Day",
    y = "Density")
```

Try a bar chart to count the number of observations by each time period. I think this would be a cool visualization to compare between time periods when we have all the data---i.e., one plot for pre-hunting, one plot for archery, and one for rifle.

I think then you would want to just plot the density plot by hour of day rather than colouring by time of day.

```{r}
ggplot(new.obs, aes(time_period, fill = time_period)) +
  geom_bar() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Time period",
    y = "Total number of observations")
```
